1.why: All seven screens use a static single-card layout with no animations, moving images, or pop-up dialogs visible.

2.why: Bold step headings and dark-teal primary buttons stand out on every screen, though the acceptance checkbox in step 6 sits oddly above its label and the required token is buried in the log panel.

3.why: Each page presents one task with one button, but the recovery token and MFA code must be located inside a monospace 'Logs' panel below the form rather than in an obvious message.

4.why: The flow is strictly linear with one action per screen and the password rule stated inline where needed, so few rules or steps must be held in memory.

5.why: No password-manager prompt, autofill hint, or 'remember me' option appears in any step; only manual pasting of the token is mentioned.

6.why: No saved or masked contact details or remembered-device cues are shown to aid recognition; only the repeated warning box and Logs panel provide any familiarity.

7.why: Instruction lines are short, but jargon such as 'non-identifying contact value,' 'recovery token,' 'MFA,' and 'mock delivery' reduces plain-language clarity.

8.why: No error messages appear in any of the seven screens, and the stated behavior is to give 'the same response whether or not it is recognized,' which neither names a problem nor explains a fix.

9.why: Steps describe what to enter (six-digit code, 12+ character password with character classes) and the Logs reveal actual values, but no concrete worked example such as a sample acceptable password is given.

10.why: Only a single authentication path (token + password + six-digit code) exists with no alternatives like face login offered, though each required input is clearly labeled.

11.why: Every screen presents exactly one input field and one primary button, so the user never faces more than one choice at a time.

12.why: Dedicated 'Sign-in confirmed' and 'Privacy conditions accepted' pages plus timestamped log entries confirm results, though intermediate steps rely on the Logs panel for feedback.

13.why: Each new step carries a short instructional line (e.g., 'You may paste or manually type the token') and a persistent 'Protect your account' tip box.

14.why: No resend, retry, or back mechanism is visible on any screen, so recovery from a mistake is not demonstrated in the shown flow.

15.why: The header, card layout, button styling, warning box, and Logs panel are identical across all seven steps, giving a highly consistent design.
